## Visualise with `timeline`

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Timeline diagram of the 423 siteswap pattern, showing the throws and catches of three props over time. Each throw is shown as an arc, with the height of the arc corresponding to the throw value. The arcs are coloured according to which prop is being thrown."
timeline(ss423)
```

## Visualise with `timeline`

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Timeline diagram of the 432 siteswap pattern, showing collisions and props appearing over time."
timeline(ss432)
```

## Visualise with `timeline` 

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Timeline diagram of the (4,4) siteswap pattern, showing the throws and catches of four props over time, with props from one hand shown as arcs above a horizontal line and props from the other hand shown as arcs below the line. The arcs are coloured according to which prop is being thrown."
ss44s <- siteswap("(4,4)")
timeline(ss44s, n_cycles = 6)
```

:::{.notes}
Different looking plot than for vanilla
:::

## Class hierarchy

```
Siteswap  
├── vanillaSiteswap
└── synchronousSiteswap
```

. . .

<br>

```{r}
ss423 <- siteswap("423")
class(ss423)
```


:::{.notes}
ss423 gets parent class and S7
:::

## Helper to assign correct class

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| label: siteswap-fn
#| code-line-numbers: "1-12|2-3|4-6"
siteswap <- function(sequence) {
  if (is_vanilla_notation(sequence)) {
    vanillaSiteswap(sequence)
  } else if (is_sync_notation(sequence)) {
    synchronousSiteswap(sequence)
  } else {
    cli::cli_abort(
      "Not valid vanilla or synchronous siteswap notation."
    )
  }
}
```

## `Siteswap` class constructor

```{r}
library(S7)
Siteswap <- new_class(
  "Siteswap",
  properties = list(
    sequence = class_character
  )
)
```


:::{.notes}
Building a simplified version of the jugglr package
:::

## `Siteswap` with property validator

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: 4-11
Siteswap <- new_class(
  "Siteswap",
  properties = list(
    sequence = new_property(
      class = class_character,
      validator = function(value) {
        if (length(value) != 1) {
          "must be length 1"
        }
      }
    )
  )
)
```


## Validation in practice

```{r}
Siteswap("423")
```


. . .

## `vanillaSiteswap` with computed properties

```{r}
#| echo: false
chr_throws_to_num <- function(throws) {
  match(tolower(throws), c(0:9, letters)) - 1
}

get_throws <- function(sequence) {
  throws_chr <- strsplit(sequence, "") |>
    unlist()

  chr_throws_to_num(throws_chr)
}

no_collisions <- function(throws) {
  n <- length(throws)
  lands <- ((seq_len(n) - 1) + throws) %% n
  anyDuplicated(lands) == 0
}

is_whole_number <- function(x) {
  x %% 1 == 0
}

is_vanilla_notation <- function(sequence) {
  stringr::str_detect(sequence, "^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$")
}
```

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: 1,3|4-10|11-16|17-22
vanillaSiteswap <- new_class(
  "vanillaSiteswap",
  parent = Siteswap,
  properties = list(
    throws = new_property(
      class = class_integer,
      getter = function(self) {
        get_throws(self@sequence) # e.g. "423" -> c(4, 2, 3)
      }
    ),
    n_props = new_property(
      class = class_numeric,
      getter = function(self) {
        mean(self@throws)
      }
    ),
    valid = new_property(
      class = class_logical,
      getter = function(self) {
        no_collisions(self@throws) && is_whole_number(self@n_props)
      }
    )
  )
)
```

:::{.notes}
Don't define a sequence property - inherits from parent Siteswap

Can use sequence value in later property definitions

Can use ealier defined properties in later prop definitions
:::

## Defining methods

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2-7"
method(print, Siteswap) <- function(x, ...) {
  if (x@valid) {
    cli::cli_bullets(c(
      "v" = "'{x@sequence}' is valid siteswap",
      "i" = "It uses {x@n_props} props"
    ))
  } else {
    cli::cli_bullets(c(
      "x" = "'{x@sequence}' is not a valid juggling pattern",
    ))
  }
}
```

:::{.notes}
print is a generic defined in base R

need same args
:::

. . .

```{r}
ss423
```


## New generic and methods

```{r}
#| eval: false
timeline <- new_generic("timeline", "siteswap")
```

:::{.notes}
"siteswap" is the dispatch argument, i.e. when `timeline` is called, it is the class of siteswap that determines which method will be used.
:::


. . .

```{r}
#| eval: false
method(timeline, vanillaSiteswap) <- function(siteswap) {
  # ggplot2 code for vanillaSiteswap timeline
}
```

. . .

```{r}
#| eval: false
method(timeline, synchronousSiteswap) <- function(siteswap) {
  # ggplot2 code for synchronousSiteswap timeline
}
```


:::{.notes}
Methods signature matches generic

Can have additional arguments
:::

## What to document and export

roxygen2 8.0.0 provides [first-class support for S7](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-S7.html).

. . .

:::{.center-h .larger200}
**[&#10003; Generics]{.pink}**
::: 

:::{.notes}
generics - list available methods
:::

. . .

:::{.center-h .larger200}
**[&#10007; Methods]{.blue}**
:::

:::{.notes}
only document individually when the method has unique behavior or arguments
:::

. . .

:::{.center-h .larger200}
**[&#10003; Classes]{.purple}**
:::

. . .

:::{.center-h .larger150}
`@param`, `@prop`
:::

:::{.notes}
classes - document the constructor
:::

:::{.notes}
In generics documentation, list methods

Is possible to document methods, but usually not necessary - definitely don't export
:::

## Registering methods: don't `@export`!

in any `.R` file (in S7 v0.2.2):

```{r}
#| eval: false
.onLoad <- function(...) {
  methods_register()
}
```


:::{.notes}
Unlike S3/S4, S7 method dispatch is not wired through NAMESPACE — it registers at load time. Without this, methods silently don't dispatch.
:::



## Order matters

- Subclass after parent class
- Methods after generic and class

```{r}
#| eval: false
# vanillaSiteswap.R

#' @include siteswap.R # contains `Siteswap`
#' @include generics.R # contains `timeline`
NULL
```

:::{.notes}
The order in which files are loaded matters - alphabetical by filename by default

Use @include

Documenting with roxygen2 then creates a `Collate` field in DESCRIPTION that ensures files load in the right order
:::

## Siteswap variations

- vanilla: **423**
- synchronous: **(4,4)(4x,4x)**
- multiplex: **[54]24**
- synchronous multiplex: **(2,6x)([6x4x],2x)**
- passing: **<3p|3p>** or **<4.5 3 3 | 3 4 3.5>**

:::{.notes}
Varies both in notation and in assumptions about how/when the props are thrown and caught
:::
